review_required.summary: item_04 and item_10 are the two numbers in the same NOAA sentence (1,000 m vs 200 m). Seeing both may read as one question answered inconsistently and induce spurious suspicion.
Seafloor-mapping percentage moves annually. Re-verify at launch; true_value and advice_value must be updated together.
The spec's 'EPR endmember ~390±5' parenthetical and its PNAS 2025 attribution could not be confirmed. Headline ~400 °C is well sourced.
2,250 m is the cited record; recent biologging tops out near 1,900 m. Debrief should call it a record, not a typical maximum.
The planted 40-year error coincides with the ~39-year counterfactual in the Cordes model. Name this in the appendix so it is not mistaken for a sourcing error.
Stem says 'longest recorded' against a 90-minute value when 117 and 138 are on record. Harmless for scoring now that this is an error item; the debrief must give both.
Smithsonian page 403s to automated fetch; value corroborated via Te Papa. Confirm the wording in a browser before the appendix.
NOAA page not directly retrieved. Value is textbook but the citation needs one manual check.

RESOLVED 2026-08-19, recorded because the diagnosis was wrong the first time. An earlier entry here claimed the bank was unbalanced 8 strong / 4 weak with advice accuracy 75% against 50%. The bank was never unbalanced: STUDY3_SPEC_v2 section 2 allocates 8 analysed items 4/4 across quality with 2 planted errors in each, plus 4 correct strong-justification fillers that exist so the error rate is 33% of twelve rather than 50% of eight. The 8/4 figure came from pipeline/analysis.py averaging fillers into the strong cell, which also recreated the base-rate confound the design avoids. Fixed by carrying role through replay.py and restricting the quality contrast to analysed items; guarded by packages/schema/test/design-constraints.test.ts and pipeline/tests/test_design_contrast.py. Cost: the correct contrast uses 4 trials per cell rather than 8 vs 4, so Var(D) rises from 0.375 to 0.500 sigma^2 and the same power needs about 33% more participants (pipeline/power.py). That is a price for removing a confound, not a regression.

No pilot data exist, so item difficulty is unmeasured. Every power figure rests on an assumed standardised effect rather than an observed SD of the discrimination score in this population, and the topic classification in items.json is a reading of the question stems rather than anything the cited sources establish. Re-estimate SD(D) from the pilot before fixing N, and state this in limitations.
